title: Snow sellers
statementMd:
The New Year celebrations in Berland last $*n*$ days. Only this year the winter is snowless, that’s why the winter celebrations’ organizers should buy artificial snow. There are $*m*$ snow selling companies in Berland. Every day the $*i*$-th company produces $*w*_{*i*}$ cubic meters of snow. Next day the snow thaws and the company has to produce $*w*_{*i*}$ cubic meters of snow again. During the celebration new year discounts are on, that’s why the snow cost decreases every day. It is known that on the first day the total cost of all the snow produced by the $*i*$-th company is equal to $*c*_{*i*}$ bourles. Every day this total cost decreases by $*a*_{*i*}$ bourles, i.e. on the second day it is equal to $*c*_{*i*} - *a*_{*i*}$,and on the third day — to $*c*_{*i*} - 2*a*_{*i*}$, and so on. It is known that for one company the cost of the snow produced by it does not get negative or equal to zero. You have to organize the snow purchase so as to buy every day exactly $*W*$ snow cubic meters. At that it is not necessary to buy from any company all the snow produced by it. If you buy $*n*_{*i*}$ cubic meters of snow ($0 ≤ *n*_{*i*} ≤ *w*_{*i*}$, the number $*n*_{*i*}$ is not necessarily integer!) from the $*i*$-th company at one of the days when the cost of its snow is equal to $*s*_{*i*}$, then its price will total to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d2154c8689d80a2d0f6cc19700d490edc9910272.png) bourles. During one day one can buy the snow from several companies. In different days one can buy the snow from different companies. It is required to make the purchases so as to spend as little money as possible. It is guaranteed that the snow produced by the companies will be enough.

## Input

The first line contains integers $*n*$, $*m*$ and $*W*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ 500000$, $1 ≤ *W* ≤ 10^{9}$) which represent the number of days, the number of companies and the amount of snow that needs to be purchased on every one of the $*n*$ days. The second line contains $*m*$ integers $*w*_{*i*}$. The third line contains $*m*$ integers $*c*_{*i*}$. The fourth line contains $*m*$ integers $*a*_{*i*}$. All the numbers are strictly positive and do not exceed $10^{9}$. For all the $*i*$ the inequation $*c*_{*i*} - (*n* - 1)*a*_{*i*} > 0$ holds true.

## Output

Print a single number — the answer to the given problem. Print the answer in the format with the decimal point (even if the answer is integer, it must contain the decimal point), without "e" and without leading zeroes. The answer should differ with the right one by no more than $10^{ - 9}$.
statementZhMd:
新年庆典在 Berland 持续 $*n*$ 天。但今年冬天没有下雪，因此冬季庆典的组织者需要购买人造雪。Berland 有 $*m*$ 家售雪公司。第 $*i*$ 家公司每天生产 $*w*_{*i*}$ 立方米的雪。第二天雪会融化，公司需要重新生产 $*w*_{*i*}$ 立方米的雪。

庆典期间有新年折扣，因此雪的价格每天都会下降。已知第一天第 $*i*$ 家公司生产的全部雪的总价为 $*c*_{*i*}$ 卢布。每天这个总价会减少 $*a*_{*i*}$ 卢布，也就是说，第二天总价为 $*c*_{*i*} - *a*_{*i*}$，第三天为 $*c*_{*i*} - 2*a*_{*i*}$，以此类推。已知对于每家公司，其生产的雪的价格不会变为负数或零。

你需要安排购买方案，使得每天恰好购买 $*W*$ 立方米的雪。不要求购买某家公司当天生产的全部雪。如果在某一天第 $*i*$ 家公司生产的雪的价格为 $*s*_{*i*}$，并从该公司购买了 $*n*_{*i*}$ 立方米的雪（$0 ≤ *n*_{*i*} ≤ *w*_{*i*}$，数量 $*n*_{*i*}$ 不一定是整数），那么需要支付的总价为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d2154c8689d80a2d0f6cc19700d490edc9910272.png) 卢布。在一天内可以从多家公司购买雪，在不同天也可以从不同公司购买雪。要求安排购买方案，使总花费尽可能少。保证各家公司生产的雪足够满足需求。

## 输入格式

第一行包含整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*W*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 500000$，$1 ≤ *W* ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示天数、公司数量以及每天需要购买的雪量。第二行包含 $*m*$ 个整数 $*w*_{*i*}$。第三行包含 $*m*$ 个整数 $*c*_{*i*}$。第四行包含 $*m*$ 个整数 $*a*_{*i*}$。所有数字均为正数且不超过 $10^{9}$。对于所有 $*i*$，均满足不等式 $*c*_{*i*} - (*n* - 1)*a*_{*i*} > 0$。

## 输出格式

输出一个数，即该问题的答案。请以带小数点的格式输出答案（即使答案是整数，也必须包含小数点），不能使用字母 "e"，且不能有前导零。输出答案与正确答案的误差不得超过 $10^{ - 9}$。
